correctness.rationale: An exact completed-square identity on the full zero-sum space reduces negative type to a 2×2 PSD test for all integers m,n>=2. At p=1 the block is positive definite; a singular determinant exists in (1,p_*). Li–Weston strict-inheritance excludes further negative-type exponents and a second root in the interval; the endpoint kernel has dimension one. Algebraic determinant rearrangement and a direct concavity estimate give strict fixed-sum balancing, while asymptotic expansions with uniform errors establish both limits. Exact-rational checker verifies 1550 finite algebraic instances, not the universal quantification.

value.rationale: The asymmetric diameter-three tree is the minimal natural nonsymmetric extension of a known sharp tree example. A strict extremal law over all leaf partitions of fixed order is a meaningful structural result. The aspect-ratio-dependent first correction and distinct fixed-small-side boundary law provide new quantitative control of snowflake Hilbert embeddability, beyond a numerical table or routine specialization.
